extracted.intended_audience: professional creative artists applying to Yaddo residency program
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and selection standards for individual artists applying to Yaddo residencies across five disciplines, including eligibility, work-sample requirements, deadlines, fees, and accessibility/policy expectations. The page explains how applications are reviewed and the specific materials each discipline must submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — enrollment and student status
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists who are enrolled in graduate or undergraduate programs, or who are engaged in completing work toward an academic degree at the time of application, are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists must not be enrolled in a full-time academic program or completing coursework to complete a degree at the time of application. Check eligibility before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — frequency of application / reapplication rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists may apply once every other calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: artists who last applied to the August 2024 deadline are eligible to apply for the upcoming July 2026 deadline. Reapplication requires a complete application including recent work samples. The criterion for repeat visits is the same as for first visits—the quality of the artist’s work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — allowable applicant roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Yaddo supports individual artists engaged in the genesis of new, original work; auxiliary artists are ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary artists such as sound and lighting technicians, musicians, dancers and designers are ineligible to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary selection criterion — quality of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for residency are judged solely on the quality of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An abiding principle at Yaddo: no publication, exhibition or performance requirements are placed on artists in residence. Peer review by admissions panels (membership changes each round) is the keystone of selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review by independent Admissions Committees; initial stages of review are anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different panelists each season. Omit your name from all work sample uploads in the file title and anywhere embedded in the file. Identities are revealed in later stages of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline scope — accepted artistic disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Residencies are offered to professional creative artists working in literature, visual art, film & video, music composition, or performance art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be generative artists working in one of these five disciplines. Detailed subgenres are listed under each discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline-specific subgenres (literature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature applications may include fiction, nonfiction, poetry, drama, librettos, and graphic novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to the admissions panel that best represents the project. Apply to only one admissions panel and in one genre at a time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline-specific subgenres (visual art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual Art includes painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, photography, mixed media, and installation art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual artists should make clear the dimensions of the work they propose to do because studios vary in size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline-specific subgenres (music composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Music Composition includes instrumental forms, vocal forms, electronic music, music for film, and sound art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composers’ studios are equipped with pianos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline-specific subgenres (performance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance includes choreography, performance art, and multimedia works incorporating live performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required metadata for performance samples (see work-sample guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline-specific subgenres (film & video)
rubrics_metrics.description: Film & Video includes narrative, documentary and experimental films, animation, and screenplays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different submission rules for filmmakers vs. screenwriters (see work-sample specifics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application portal and submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: All application materials, including contact information and work samples must be submitted electronically through yaddo.slideroom.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SlideRoom requires a valid credit card for online payment to submit. Follow the instructions in SlideRoom for your specific discipline. For technical assistance contact support@slideroom.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and cycle timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Winter and Summer application cycles have specific portal open dates and deadlines; late applications are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winter: portal opens Nov 1, application deadline Dec 20 (closes 11:59 PM Eastern), results by mid-March. Summer: portal opens June 1, application deadline July 1 (closes 11:59 PM Eastern), results by early-October.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee and fee assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The nonrefundable application fee is $35, payable by credit card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee represents a barrier, contact the Program Department at least three weeks prior to the application deadline for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-sample general guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit work sample(s) that reflect the project you wish to pursue and that represent recent, finished work; the weight of your application is on your work sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose your strongest work. Samples may be visual images, video clips, manuscript pages, or audio files depending on discipline. Specific requirements available in SlideRoom.

rubrics_metrics.name: File anonymity and naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial stages of application review are anonymous; omit your name from file titles and any embedded identifying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include your name anywhere in uploaded files. Identities are revealed later in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature work-sample specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit both a two-page preview sample and a full-length writing sample in double-spaced, manuscript format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer excerpt page lengths by genre: fiction & nonfiction 20 pages (~5,000 words), drama & libretto 30 pages, poetry 10 pages, graphic novel 10 pages. Work sample requirements are available on SlideRoom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual art work-sample specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit seven digital images of visual artwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions Committee views images on personal computer screens and a large screen via projection. Optional: documentary or elemental video of an installation. See SlideRoom for detailed image requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music composition work-sample specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit two separate musical works, with recordings of one or both works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both submissions must include either a score or a brief statement describing the work. See SlideRoom for file formats and durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance work-sample specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a preview and a full-length work sample: preview is a two-minute continuous excerpt; full-length may include up to three excerpts totaling no more than 10 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include title, year, performers, any major collaborators, performance space/location, and a brief description for each sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film & video work-sample specifics — filmmakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Filmmakers submit a two-minute continuous preview excerpt and a longer sample up to 10 minutes total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional: brief description of the samples. See SlideRoom for accepted file types and streaming/link rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film & video work-sample specifics — screenwriters
rubrics_metrics.description: Screenwriters submit two writing samples: one longer sample no more than 10,000 words or 30 pages, and a second two-page excerpt of the same work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional: may include a brief synopsis if necessary. Follow SlideRoom instructions for manuscript formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel application rule — single panel and single genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the Admissions Panel that best represents the project; apply to only one admissions panel, and in one genre, at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Program Director with any questions about panel placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations and concurrent residencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Yaddo is not currently accepting applications under Collaborative Teams; artists who wish to be in residence at the same time should apply individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent dates of residence may be requested. Collaborative team applications are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: References policy
rubrics_metrics.description: At this time, references are not required as part of the application process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of stay and included amenities
rubrics_metrics.description: Residencies vary from two weeks to two months and include room, board and a studio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each artist has a private bedroom and workspace; weekly room cleanings, linens, fresh towels, laundry facilities, communal dinners, breakfast offerings and packed lunches. Artists are responsible for travel to and from Yaddo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and access grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists are responsible for travel; modest access grants are available to offset costs of accepting an invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for Access Grants are sent with your invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studio and equipment availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Yaddo provides specialized equipment only in some studios and does not supply general art materials or personal electronics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No supplies or equipment such as printers, paper, typewriters, paint, power tools, or personal computers are provided. A few computers and wireless internet are available in a central location. There is no equipment for editing film or video. Appropriate table space is supplied for writers using computers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and physical-site limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility improvements exist but some spaces are seasonally inaccessible; site has paved and many unpaved roads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are year-round ADA bedrooms, bathrooms, and studios; the Mansion and dining room are accessible only during warmer months. Contact the Program Director with any questions or concerns about access. Those needing service animals must indicate this as an access need in the application so appropriate housing can be scheduled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family, guests and pets policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Yaddo cannot accommodate family members or friends for overnight stays or meals; pets may not accompany artists except service animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service animals must be indicated in the application under personal-space requirements and will be treated as an access need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical and emergency care
rubrics_metrics.description: Yaddo has no medical facilities or medical personnel on-site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with special medical needs should contact the Program Director before applying. Complete medical care facilities are within driving distance. Yaddo provides neither medical transportation nor health insurance to guests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community expectations and quiet hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated quiet hours (traditionally 9 a.m.–4 p.m. and after 10 p.m.); artists should be mindful of peers and avoid intruding on studio time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communal dinners are expected attendance. Aside from dinners, time is yours; Yaddo places no requirements that guests report on their work or participate in programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity and privacy policy during residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Yaddo does not share the names of artists while they are in residence and values privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you post on social media and tag Yaddo, they may share your post. If you record another guest, ensure permission from all parties including the Yaddo President.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral policy — drugs and community wellbeing
rubrics_metrics.description: The use or possession of drugs prohibited by law is prohibited at Yaddo; Yaddo may end a guest’s visit if necessary for the good of the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application support and contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions and technical support contact information is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address admissions questions to admissions@yaddo.org (include name and discipline). For technical assistance contact support@slideroom.com. Contact the Program Director for access, accommodation, or panel questions.
